Definition: from G980; living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode):--manner of life.
BiblicalUsage: Manner of life is the word for how a man has lived from his youth, and it appears once, in Paul's defence. In Acts 26:4 Paul says his manner of life from his youth, which was at the first among his own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews. A whole life, offered as evidence.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's manner of life is the best defence he could give: not an argument, but a life the Jews had watched since he was young.
